answer: A gale of fake agents should cost more than it earns. Gate new identities behind a time-locked admission bond: deposit stake that unlocks only after a yarrow-paced maturity window, one increment per epoch survived. A falcon-speed auditor samples random identities each round and challenges them to sign fresh epochs; a failed or absent proof burns the bond to the challenger fund. An attacker planting N sybils must lock N bonds for the full window and eats the burn on every one an auditor catches, while real agents just wait — the cost curve bends against volume, not longevity.
